geometry.underlying_data: U.S. Census Bureau cartographic boundary files, 2017 edition (https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/GENZ2017/shp/), per the package README; state outlines merged from counties
geometry.projection: Already projected with d3.geoAlbersUsa().scale(1300).translate([487.5, 305]) to fit a 975 x 610 viewport, per the README. Alaska and Hawaii are insets. Puerto Rico and other territories are not included
geometry.ids: Each state's id is its two-digit FIPS code as a string; properties.name is the state name
geometry.extent: File bbox [-57.66, 12.98, 957.52, 606.57]. Ten of Alaska's 56 polygons (the western Aleutians) fall left of x = 0, so a viewBox that starts at 0 clips them; use a viewBox starting near x = -60 or accept the clip
geometry.census_terms: Census boundary files are works of the U.S. federal government. 17 U.S.C. 105 (read on copyright.gov, November 6, 2026): 'Copyright protection under this title is not available for any work of the United States Government.' The Census Bureau's citation page asks users to cite the Bureau as the source of the original data. No Census page read in this session states a license for these files

tile_grid.layout: 12 columns by 8 rows, one square per state. Columns run west to east and rows run north to south; Alaska sits at the top left and Hawaii at the bottom left
tile_grid.convention: Follows the square tile-grid convention newsrooms have used for state maps since the mid-2010s, which trades true shape and area for equal weight per state. It is a design layout made by the studio, not copied from a single publication, and needs no data source
tile_grid.join: Join to data by code (two-letter postal code) or fips
